claim: A high density of Na+ channels at nodes of Ranvier is necessary for rapid and efficient action potential propagation in myelinated axons.
source: A high density of Na+ channels at nodes of Ranvier is necessary for rapid and efficient action potential propagation in myelinated axons.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific experimental data in this manuscript.

claim: Na+ channels cluster at nodes in the absence of NF186.
source: Here we show that while Na+ channels cluster at nodes in the absence of NF186, they fail to do so in double conditional knockout mice lacking both NF186 and the paranodal cell adhesion molecule Caspr
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from conditional knockout mice shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Na+ channels fail to cluster in double conditional knockout mice lacking both NF186 and Caspr.
source: Here we show that while Na+ channels cluster at nodes in the absence of NF186, they fail to do so in double conditional knockout mice lacking both NF186 and the paranodal cell adhesion molecule Caspr
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from double knockout mice shown in Figure 3.

claim: Paranode-dependent clustering of nodal Na+ channels requires axonal βII spectrin.
source: Furthermore, we show that paranode-dependent clustering of nodal Na+ channels requires axonal βII spectrin which is concentrated at paranodes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from double knockout mice lacking NF186 and βII spectrin shown in Figure 4.

claim: The paranodal junction-dependent mechanism of Na+ channel clustering is mediated by the spectrin-based paranodal axonal cytoskeleton.
source: Our results reveal that the paranodal junction-dependent mechanism of Na+channel clustering is mediated by the spectrin-based paranodal axonal cytoskeleton.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the experimental data showing loss of Na+ channel clustering in mice lacking both NF186 and βII spectrin.

claim: The Nfasc gene is alternatively spliced to generate a neuronal 186 kDa variant (NF186) found at nodes of Ranvier.
source: The Nfasc gene is alternatively spliced to generate a neuronal 186 kDa variant (NF186) found at nodes of Ranvier (Davis et al., 1996)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The Nfasc gene is alternatively spliced to generate a glial 155 kDa variant (NF155) that is a core component of the paranodal junctions.
source: a glial 155 kDa variant (NF155) that is a core component of the paranodal junctions (Tait et al., 2000; Pillai et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Genetic deletion of both NF155 and NF186 in mice results in the absence of nodal Na+ channel clusters.
source: Nfasc is essential for node of Ranvier assembly as genetic deletion of both NF155 and NF186 in mice results in the absence of nodal Na+ channel clusters (Sherman et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: NF186 is clustered and stabilized at the axolemma by glial adhesion molecules and extracellular matrix at peripheral and central nodes.
source: At peripheral (PNS) and central (CNS) nodes, NF186 is clustered and stabilized at the axolemma by glial adhesion molecules and extracellular matrix (ECM) (Eshed et al., 2005; Feinberg et al., 2010; Susuki et al., 2013; Colombelli et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Clustered NF186 functions as an attachment site for the nodal scaffolding proteins ankyrinG (AnkG) and βIV spectrin, which in turn recruit Na+ channels.
source: Clustered NF186 functions as an attachment site for the nodal scaffolding proteins ankyrinG (AnkG) and βIV spectrin, which in turn recruit Na+ channels (Davis and Bennett, 1994; Sherman et al., 2005; Yang et al., 2007; Gasser et al., 2012; Ho et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: NF186 helps to stabilize and maintain the nodal Na+ channel protein complex after node assembly.
source: After node assembly, NF186 helps to stabilize and maintain the nodal Na+ channel protein complex (Amor et al., 2014; Desmazieres et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Transgenic expression of neuronal NF186 on an Nfasc-null background is sufficient to rescue nodal Na+ channel clustering.
source: Consistent with these observations, transgenic expression of neuronal NF186 on an Nfasc-null background is sufficient to rescue nodal Na+ channel clustering (Zonta et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The glial NF155-dependent paranodal axoglial junctions function as lateral diffusion barriers to restrict the location of nodal proteins in the axolemma.
source: In addition, the glial NF155-dependent paranodal axoglial junctions have also been proposed to function as a parallel mechanism to cluster Na+ channels by acting as lateral diffusion barriers to restrict the location of nodal proteins in the axolemma (Rasband et al., 1999; Pedraza et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Transgenic expression of NF155 in myelinating oligodendrocytes on a Nfasc-null background is sufficient to induce Na+ channel clustering.
source: In support of this idea, transgenic expression of NF155 in myelinating oligodendrocytes on a Nfasc-null background is sufficient to induce Na+ channel clustering (Zonta et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: In vitro myelination of Nfasc-null axons by wild-type Schwann cells induces the clustering of Na+ channels at nodes.
source: Similarly, in vitro myelination of Nfasc-null axons by wild-type Schwann cells (which results in the formation of a normal paranodal junction) induces the clustering of Na+ channels at nodes (Feinberg et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Mice lacking both paranodal junctions and NF186-binding CNS nodal ECM proteins have a profound reduction in the clustering of Na+ channels.
source: Furthermore, mice lacking both paranodal junctions and NF186-binding CNS nodal ECM proteins have a profound reduction in the clustering of Na+ channels (Susuki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Disruption of paranodal junctions alone causes only mild perturbations to Na+ channel clustering.
source: In contrast, disruption of paranodal junctions alone causes only mild perturbations to Na+ channel clustering (Dupree et al., 1999; Bhat et al., 2001; Boyle et al., 2001; Pillai et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Conditional deletion of NF186 in neurons was reported to block the clustering of Na+ channels at nodes of Ranvier.
source: Nevertheless, this model, and in particular the function of the paranodal junction in the clustering of Na+ channels, remains controversial since conditional deletion of NF186 in neurons was reported to block the clustering of Na+ channels at nodes of Ranvier (Thaxton et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Immunoblots of brain lysates derived from postnatal day 6 (P6) Pgk-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice showed no immunoreactivity for Nfasc gene products.
source: Immunoblots of brain lysates derived from postnatal day 6 (P6) Pgk-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice showed no immunoreactivity for Nfasc gene products (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Pgk-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice died within a few days of birth.
source: Consistent with the previously reported Nfasc-null mice (Sherman et al., 2005), Pgk-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice died within a few days of birth
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental animals.

claim: Immunostaining of sciatic nerves from Pgk-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice showed neither paranodal junctions nor Na+ channel clustering.
source: immunostaining of sciatic nerves showed neither paranodal junctions nor Na+ channel clustering (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c and d).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1c and d.

claim: Avil-Cre mice restrict Cre-mediated recombination to PNS sensory neurons beginning at E12.5.
source: we crossed Nfascfl/fl mice with Avil-Cre mice (Hasegawa et al., 2007; Zhou et al., 2010), which restricts the Cre-mediated recombination to PNS sensory neurons beginning at E12.5.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work describing the Avil-Cre mouse line.

claim: Immunostaining of dorsal roots from Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice showed complete loss of nodal NF186.
source: Immunostaining of dorsal roots from Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice using a neurofascin antibody that recognizes all splice variants (panNF) showed complete loss of nodal NF186
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Paranodal junctions are preserved in dorsal roots from Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice as indicated by Caspr and paranodal panNF immunostaining.
source: but preserved paranodal junctions as indicated by Caspr and paranodal panNF immunostaining (Figure 1a)
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Transmission electron microscopy on dorsal roots from Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice found no disruption of the paranodal junctions.
source: To determine if the paranodal junctions are intact in Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice we performed transmission electron microscopy on dorsal roots and found no disruption of the junctions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1e.

claim: Na+ channels cluster at all nodes of Ranvier in dorsal roots from Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice at both P9 and P12.
source: We found clusters of Na+ channels at all nodes of Ranvier at both P9 and P12 (Figure 1b–d).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 1b-d.

claim: Na+ channels, AnkG, and βIV spectrin were unaffected by the loss of NF186 in Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice.
source: Whereas Na+ channels, AnkG, and βIV spectrin were unaffected by the loss of NF186
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Gldn was no longer restricted to nodes of Ranvier in Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice.
source: Gldn was no longer restricted to nodes of Ranvier, consistent with gliomedin's function as a ligand for NF186 (Eshed et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1c and a citation to previous work.

claim: Analysis of peripheral nerves from Thy1-Cre;Nfasc(4)fl/fl mice revealed clustered Na+ channels, AnkG, and βIV spectrin, but loss of the nodal NF186 ligands NrCAM and Gldn.
source: Similar to Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice, analysis of peripheral nerves from Thy1-Cre;Nfasc(4)fl/fl mice revealed clustered Na+ channels, AnkG, and βIV spectrin, but loss of the nodal NF186 ligands NrCAM and Gldn (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b and d).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2b and d.

claim: 84% of heminodes from wild-type cultures had heminodal Na+ channel clusters.
source: Whereas 84% (n = 128 heminodes) of heminodes from wild-type (WT) cultures had heminodal Na+ channel clusters (Figure 1e)
evidence: This is supported by quantification of immunostaining data from DRG cultures.

claim: Only 6% of heminodes from Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice had heminodal Na+ channel clusters.
source: only 6% (n = 113 heminodes) of heminodes from Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice had heminodal Na+ channel clusters.
evidence: This is supported by quantification of immunostaining data from DRG cultures.

claim: The intensity of nodal Na+ channel staining was reduced in Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl dorsal roots.
source: Intriguingly, close examination of Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl dorsal roots and Thy1-Cre;Nfasc(4)fl/fl peripheral nerves showed that the intensity of nodal Na+ channel staining was reduced (Figure 1b and Figure 1—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1b and Figure 1—figure supplement 2b.

claim: Quantification of the nodal Na+ channel fluorescence intensity in Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice at P9 and P12 showed a significant reduction compared to control Nfascfl/fl mice.
source: Quantification of the nodal Na+ channel fluorescence intensity in Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice at P9 and P12 showed a significant reduction compared to control Nfascfl/fl mice (Figure 1f).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: Compound action potential recordings from P10 dorsal roots revealed a reduction in conduction velocity in Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice.
source: Consistent with this reduced nodal Na+ channel density, compound action potential recordings from P10 dorsal roots (Figure 1—figure supplement 1f) revealed a reduction in conduction velocity in Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1g).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1f and 1g.

claim: Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice began to develop a progressive tremor at 7–10 days that worsened until most mice died at around 3 weeks of age.
source: The loss of Na+ channels from nodes may account for the juvenile lethality observed in Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice (i.e., at 7–10 days these mice began to develop a progressive tremor that worsened until most mice died at around 3 weeks of age).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental animals.

claim: Six3-Cre mice undergo recombination in retinal ganglion cells.
source: we crossed Nfascfl/fl mice with Six3-Cre mice which are reported to undergo recombination in retinal ganglion cells (Furuta et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work describing the Six3-Cre mouse line.

claim: Some oligodendrocytes in the Six3-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mouse also recombine, resulting in a mosaic nerve with some regions lacking both NF155 and NF186.
source: However, we found that some oligodendrocytes in the Six3-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mouse also recombine, resulting in a mosaic nerve with some regions lacking both NF155 and NF186 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–b, outlined region).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1a-b.

claim: Regions lacking both NF155 and NF186 had dramatically reduced Na+ channel clustering.
source: Like Pgk-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice, regions lacking both NF155 and NF186 had dramatically reduced Na+ channel clustering
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1b.

claim: When Na+ channels were clustered in regions lacking paranodal NF155, they always colocalized with NF186 in axons corresponding to retinal ganglion cells that presumably did not undergo recombination.
source: when Na+ channels were clustered in regions lacking paranodal NF155, they always colocalized with NF186 in axons corresponding to retinal ganglion cells that presumably did not undergo recombination (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Robust Na+ channel clustering was found in the gap between all panNF-labeled paranodal junctions at P17 and P30 in the Six3-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mouse optic nerve.
source: Consistent with our observations in the PNS, we found robust Na+ channel clustering in the gap between all panNF-labeled paranodal junctions at P17 and P30 in the Six3-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mouse optic nerve (Figure 2a,b,d).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 2a, b, and d.

claim: At P60 some nodes in Six3-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice had intact panNF-labeled paranodal junctions but without any associated Na+ channel immunostaining.
source: Intriguingly, at P60 some nodes had intact panNF-labeled paranodal junctions but without any associated Na+ channel immunostaining (Figure 2c, arrowhead and Figure 2d).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 2c and d.

claim: In contrast to the PNS, a general reduction in Na+ channel fluorescence intensities was not observed in the CNS of Six3-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice.
source: However, in contrast to the PNS (Figure 1f), we did not observe a general reduction in Na+ channel fluorescence intensities (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: Nodes lacking NF186 in the Six3-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice had AnkG and βIV spectrin.
source: As expected, nodes lacking NF186 in the Six3-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice had AnkG and βIV spectrin (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1c.

claim: No invasion of Kv1.2-subunit containing K+ channels into paranodal regions was observed in the Six3-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mouse optic nerve, indicating that the paranodal axoglial junctions remain intact.
source: Furthermore, we did not observe any invasion of Kv1.2-subunit containing K+ channels into paranodal regions, indicating that the paranodal axoglial junctions remain intact in the Six3-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mouse optic nerve (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Analysis of nodes of Ranvier in the spinal cords of Thy1-Cre;Nfasc(4)fl/fl showed robust clustering of Na+ channels, AnkG, and βIV spectrin despite the loss of NF186.
source: Similarly, analysis of nodes of Ranvier in the spinal cords of Thy1-Cre;Nfasc(4)fl/fl showed that despite the loss of NF186, there was robust clustering of Na+ channels, AnkG, and βIV spectrin (Figure 1—figure supplement 2c and d).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2c and d.

claim: The chondroitin-sulfate proteoglycan brevican (Bcan) could not be detected in the spinal cords of Thy1-Cre;Nfasc(4)fl/fl mice.
source: However, the chondroitin-sulfate proteoglycan brevican (Bcan), a core nodal ECM protein that binds to NF186 (Susuki et al., 2013), could not be detected (Figure 1—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2c and a citation to previous work.

claim: Compound action potential recordings from Six3-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mouse optic nerves showed a significant reduction in conduction velocity at all time points analyzed.
source: Similar to our observations in the PNS, compound action potential recordings from Nfascfl/fl and Six3-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mouse optic nerves showed a significant reduction in conduction velocity at all time points analyzed (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d and 1e).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d and 1e.

claim: The reduced conduction velocity in Six3-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice does not reflect impaired myelination.
source: The reduced conduction velocity does not reflect impaired myelination (Figure 2—figure supplement 1f and 1g)
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1f and 1g.

claim: The reduced conduction velocity in Six3-Cre;Nfascfl/fl mice likely reflects the combined effects of decreased nodal Na+ channel density, loss of nodal extracellular matrix molecules, and loss of some paranodal junctions due to NF155-deficient oligodendrocytes.
source: but instead likely reflects the combined effects of decreased nodal Na+ channel density, loss of nodal extracellular matrix molecules (Weber et al., 1999; Bekku et al., 2010), and loss of some paranodal junctions due to NF155-deficient oligodendrocytes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and citations to previous work.

claim: Immunostaining of dorsal roots from Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl;Casprfl/fl mice showed complete loss of Caspr-labeled paranodal junctions and nodal NF186.
source: Immunostaining of dorsal roots from Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl;Casprfl/fl mice showed complete loss of Caspr-labeled paranodal junctions and nodal NF186
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: A redistribution of Kv1.1 K+ channels into paranodal regions was observed in Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl;Casprfl/fl mice.
source: as well as a redistribution of Kv1.1 K+ channels into paranodal regions (Figure 3b, arrowheads).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: Immunostaining for Nav1.6 Na+ channels or βIV spectrin showed a complete loss of clustering of these nodal proteins in Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl;Casprfl/fl mice.
source: Furthermore, immunostaining for Nav1.6 Na+ channels or βIV spectrin showed a complete loss of clustering of these nodal proteins (Figure 3c,d).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3c and d.

claim: Loss of both NF186 and the paranodal axoglial junctions blocks the assembly of nodes.
source: Thus, loss of both NF186 and the paranodal axoglial junctions blocks the assembly of nodes, confirming that intact paranodes function as a second, independent mechanism for Na+ channel clustering.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The enrichment of AnkG in the axon initial segment (AIS) depends on an αII/βII spectrin-dependent submembranous cytoskeleton that functions as an intra-axonal boundary.
source: We previously showed that the enrichment of AnkG in the axon initial segment (AIS) depends on an αII/βII spectrin-dependent submembranous cytoskeleton that functions as an intra-axonal boundary (Galiano et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Paranodes have a specialized αII/βII spectrin-based axonal cytoskeleton whose assembly requires the NF155-dependent paranodal junction.
source: Paranodes also have a specialized αII/βII spectrin-based axonal cytoskeleton whose assembly requires the NF155-dependent paranodal junction (Ogawa et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: 94.1% of nodes in control mice had clustered Na+ channels.
source: Importantly, 94.1% and 94.6% of nodes in control and Avil-Cre; Sptbn1fl/fl mice, respectively, had clustered Na+ channels (p=0.28 by Student's t-test; n = 3 independent animals for each genotype and a total of 796 and 464 nodes were examined in control and cKO mice, respectively).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of immunostaining data.

claim: 94.6% of nodes in Avil-Cre;Sptbn1fl/fl mice had clustered Na+ channels.
source: Importantly, 94.1% and 94.6% of nodes in control and Avil-Cre; Sptbn1fl/fl mice, respectively, had clustered Na+ channels (p=0.28 by Student's t-test; n = 3 independent animals for each genotype and a total of 796 and 464 nodes were examined in control and cKO mice, respectively).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of immunostaining data.

claim: Avil-Cre;Sptbn1fl/fl mice have normal Na+ channel clustering and densities of Na+ channels.
source: Thus, Avil-Cre;Sptbn1fl/fl mice have normal Na+ channel clustering and densities of Na+ channels, indicating that NF186 is sufficient to cluster nodal Na+ channels.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the quantification data.

claim: Animals lacking both NF186 and βII spectrin in their sensory axons had an extreme deficit in proprioception.
source: Compared to single knockouts (Figure 1 and (Zhang et al., 2013) and Nfascfl/f;Sptbn1fl/fl mice), animals lacking both NF186 and βII spectrin in their sensory axons had an extreme deficit in proprioception (Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral observation shown in Video 1 and comparison to single knockouts.

claim: Electron microscopy showed paranodes, but thinner myelin in Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl;Sptbn1fl/fl mice.
source: Electron microscopy showed paranodes, but thinner myelin in Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl;Sptbn1fl/fl mice (Figure 4a–d)
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 4a-d.

claim: Mice lacking βII spectrin had normal myelination.
source: whereas mice lacking βII spectrin had normal myelination (Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Both Nfascfl/fl and Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl;Sptbn1fl/fl mice had normal paranodal Caspr.
source: To confirm that paranodal junctions are intact we immunostained paranodes in dorsal roots using antibodies to Caspr. Both Nfascfl/fl and Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl;Sptbn1fl/fl mice had normal paranodal Caspr (Figure 4e), indicating intact paranodal junctions.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: Immunostaining of roots lacking NF186 and βII spectrin revealed a profound loss of Na+ channel, AnkG, and βIV spectrin clustering at P10 and P15 despite intact NF155-dependent paranodal junctions.
source: Nevertheless, immunostaining of roots lacking NF186 and βII spectrin revealed a profound loss of Na+ channel, AnkG, and βIV spectrin clustering (Figure 4F–I) at P10 and P15 despite intact NF155-dependent paranodal junctions.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4f-i.

claim: Two glia-dependent mechanisms direct Na+ channel clustering at nodes of Ranvier.
source: Our results confirm and extend the model that two glia-dependent mechanisms direct Na+ channel clustering at nodes of Ranvier (Feinberg et al., 2010; Susuki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The two mechanisms for Na+ channel clustering consist of: (1) glia-derived adhesion/ECM proteins working through NF186, and (2) the assembly of a paranodal junction dependent cytoskeletal barrier containing βII spectrin.
source: These mechanisms consist of: (1) glia-derived adhesion/ECM proteins working through NF186, and (2) the assembly of a paranodal junction dependent cytoskeletal barrier containing βII spectrin (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and illustrated in Figure 5A.

claim: These two mechanisms converge on the clustering of the axonal cytoskeletal scaffolding proteins AnkG and βIV spectrin at the nodes of Ranvier.
source: These two mechanisms converge on the clustering of the axonal cytoskeletal scaffolding proteins AnkG and βIV spectrin at the nodes of Ranvier (Ho et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The loss of NF186 can be partially compensated for by the paranodal junction-based cytoskeletal barrier since Na+ channels may still be clustered, but they cannot be maintained in the absence of NF186.
source: Accordingly, the loss of NF186 can be partially compensated for by the paranodal junction-based cytoskeletal barrier since Na+ channels may still be clustered, but they cannot be maintained in the absence of NF186 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and illustrated in Figure 5B.

claim: Na+ channels still cluster at nodes in the absence of the paranodal junction barrier due to the function of NF186 at the forming nodes.
source: With the same rationale, Na+ channels still cluster at nodes in the absence of the paranodal junction barrier (by genetically deleting cell adhesion molecules that mediate axoglial contact at this site (Bhat et al., 2001; Boyle et al., 2001; Pillai et al., 2009), or βII spectrin [Zhang et al., 2013]) due to the function of NF186 at the forming nodes (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data, citations to previous work, and illustrated in Figure 5C.

claim: When both NF186 and the paranodal junction based spectrin cytoskeleton are lost, Na+ channels cannot be clustered at nodes.
source: When both NF186 and the paranodal junction based spectrin cytoskeleton are lost, Na+ channels cannot be clustered at nodes (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and illustrated in Figure 5D.

claim: Glial NF155 binds to a heterodimeric cell adhesion molecule complex consisting of axonal Caspr and contactin.
source: Glial NF155 binds to a heterodimeric cell adhesion molecule complex consisting of axonal Caspr and contactin (Charles et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: In myelinating glia, NF155 interacts with ankyrinB (AnkB) and AnkG to facilitate the assembly of the paranodal junction, which in turn controls the rapid development of Na+ channel clustering in the CNS.
source: In myelinating glia, NF155 also interacts with ankyrinB (AnkB) and AnkG to facilitate the assembly of the paranodal junction, which in turn controls the rapid development of Na+ channel clustering in the CNS (Chang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Axonal Caspr has a cytoplasmic protein 4.1 binding domain.
source: Axonal Caspr has a cytoplasmic protein 4.1 binding domain
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Protein 4.1B is enriched at paranodes and juxtaparanodes.
source: and protein 4.1B is enriched at paranodes and juxtaparanodes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Protein 4.1B binds to αII/βII spectrin.
source: Protein 4.1B binds to αII/βII spectrin
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Mice deficient in either 4.1B or βII spectrin have impaired axonal membrane domain organization with mislocalization of juxtaparanodal Kv1 K+ channels due to loss of the paranodal boundary.
source: and mice deficient in either 4.1B or βII spectrin have impaired axonal membrane domain organization with mislocalization of juxtaparanodal Kv1 K+ channels due to loss of the paranodal boundary (Horresh et al., 2010; Einheber et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In myelinated axons, glial NF155 directs the assembly of the αII/βII spectrin-based paranodal cytoskeleton through Caspr and protein 4.1B.
source: Together, these observations suggest that in myelinated axons, glial NF155 directs the assembly of the αII/βII spectrin-based paranodal cytoskeleton through Caspr and protein 4.1B.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and previous work.

claim: Mice lacking both NF186 and protein 4.1B should phenocopy the Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl;Sptbn1fl/fl mice.
source: One prediction from this model is that mice lacking both NF186 and protein 4.1B should phenocopy the Avil-Cre;Nfascfl/fl;Sptbn1fl/fl mice we analyzed.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the proposed model.

claim: Similar to the AIS and distal axon, different spectrin and ankyrin cytoskeletons occupy mutually exclusive domains due to steric effects.
source: We speculate that similar to the AIS and distal axon (Galiano et al., 2012), different spectrin and ankyrin cytoskeletons occupy mutually exclusive domains due to steric effects.
evidence: This is speculation based on previous work.

claim: Domains containing βIV spectrin are mutually exclusive to those containing βII spectrin.
source: Thus, domains containing βIV spectrin are mutually exclusive to those containing βII spectrin.
evidence: This is speculation based on the proposed model.

claim: The βII spectrin-based cytoskeleton in unmyelinated axons is organized into repeating rings of spectrin tetramers and actin.
source: Recent experiments using super-resolution microscopy reveal that the βII spectrin-based cytoskeleton in unmyelinated axons is organized into repeating rings of spectrin tetramers and actin (Xu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The high density of αII/βII spectrin found at paranodes may not be organized in the same way as in unmyelinated axons.
source: However, the high density of αII/βII spectrin found at paranodes may not be organized in the same way
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation of high spectrin density at paranodes.

claim: The high density of αII/βII spectrin at paranodes may function to restrict ankG/βIV spectrin-containing cytoskeletons to the forming nodes as the myelin sheath elongates.
source: and this high density may function to restrict ankG/βIV spectrin-containing cytoskeletons to the forming nodes as the myelin sheath elongates.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of action.

claim: The conclusion that the paranodal junction contributes to the clustering of nodal Na+ channels is consistent with previous studies.
